name: Graph Signal Denoising and Trend Filtering
problem_statement: Estimate a vertex signal from noisy observations using a declared graph-difference regularizer.

normalization: Preserve all declared vertices, including isolated vertices.
Preserve direction; an undirected projection must be explicitly requested.
Declare the treatment of self-loops and parallel edges before execution; an adapter must reject unsupported cases.

problem_inputs.name: observed_signal
problem_inputs.description: Scalar or fixed-width vector observations per vertex.

problem_inputs.name: regularizer
problem_inputs.description: Total variation, higher-order trend filtering or quadratic Laplacian smoothing.

required_outputs.name: objective_value
required_outputs.description: Declared objective evaluated on the returned signal.

required_outputs.name: converged
required_outputs.description: Whether the declared solver tolerance was met.

solution_semantics.objective: Minimize squared observation error plus the declared graph-difference penalty.
solution_semantics.exactness: Numerical optimization with disclosed stopping conditions; different regularizers define different variants.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Output identities refer to the normalized input; any multiplicities must follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No output order or choice among equally valid optima is required unless specified by an input.

validation_rules: Recompute the stated objective and convergence residual.
With zero regularization the solution equals observations.
Compare small instances with an independent convex solver.
edge_cases: Isolated vertices retain their observations for edge-difference penalties.
Disconnected components can be processed independently.

correctness: Recompute the stated objective and convergence residual.
With zero regularization the solution equals observations.
Compare small instances with an independent convex solver.
